title: Team communications — one capability across three builds, one of them not on the tenant API
why: Six inventory rows describe one thing a user would name once: the same ATeamChat component in three HTML builds (`app.html` S-040, `app-tenant.html` S-142, `maya-os-site/index.html` S-100), plus two parts of the `app.html` one — the `?team=main` deep-link mount (S-064) and its voice recorder (S-282) — and the NestJS controller the `app.html` copy posts to (S-272, a `team-communications.controller.ts` file carried in the inventory as channel `pwa`, kind `notification`). The deep-link overlay is not a convenience added because the tab was hard to reach: its own anchor (L33983) sits in AStaffDashboard, which the router never renders — `window.ALivePanel` is always assigned (L37629) and wins the `panel` fallback (L39152) — so in `app.html` the team surface is reached only by a hand-typed `?team=main` URL, which S-272 describes as a surface nobody finds by design. The three copies are also not in the same position, and the difference decides the size of the job: S-100 records that its copy runs on the legacy МЭ proxy (L34866) rather than the tenant API and states in its own words that a merge there is a rebuild, not a re-parent, while the `app.html` copy already talks to the tenant controller (S-272 L22-74; S-282's chunked upload path). In a chat-first rebuild where primary navigation collapses from 112 reachable surfaces to five destinations, this belongs in one authority-scoped lane of the single conversation surface — with MAYA present rather than adjacent — not in a second, hidden chat application.
disappear: The `?team=main` deep-link mount with its independent ReactDOM root, the duplicate ATeamChat copies in the other two builds, the staff message feed as a surface of its own, and the standalone voice recorder as a surface of its own. One primary-navigation entry goes with them — the team tab in `app-tenant.html` (S-142, `STAFF_TABS` index 3, L21844); the other five rows are sub-states beneath primary navigation rather than entries in it. What disappears is the surface count, not the behaviour behind it: S-064 requires that the `?team=main` URL keep resolving after the merge, and that the merge target supply a real entry point rather than only absorbing the code. Nothing disappears before parity — all six rows are RETIRE AFTER PARITY at K16, and all six successor cells still read `MERGE_TARGET — the surface it folds into, to be named` (source: REQUIRES SIGNATURE), so the single lane described here is the recommendation being signed, not a destination that already exists.
remain: Hold-to-record voice with slide-to-cancel and swipe-up lock (S-100 L34890-34893), media attachments with upload progress (L34894-34896), the media viewer (L34896), TCVoice playback (L34383), attachments up to 20 MB (S-142) with message withdraw and delete (S-040, S-142), chunked attachment upload with per-chunk receipt verification to `/team-communications/attachments/<id>/chunks/<i>` (S-272, S-282), and the 10-second feed poll (S-272 L38314). Presence and typing indicators are evidenced only for the `maya-os-site` copy (S-100 L34897-34898) — for the `app.html` and `app-tenant.html` copies "remain" means "build". The controller's `@Roles` list (TENANT_OWNER, BUSINESS_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN, ADMINISTRATOR, STAFF) must be carried into the lane selector and stay enforced where it is enforced today, on the server; S-272 states it is the only thing keeping staff traffic out of client threads.
risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — above the MEDIUM the group line carried, below G01's statutory HIGH, because three hazards outrank the upload path the old line named. First, the 152-ФЗ boundary: merging human-to-human and human-to-AI chat into one shell without unmistakable provenance lets a master post a client's personal data into a thread they believe is internal (S-142), and the standing rule is that client PD never reaches the LLM. Second, the recorder: it tears its streams down on unmount (S-282 L38314), so a lane that mounts and unmounts with messages risks leaving a live microphone open; its iOS-first MIME order ['audio/mp4','audio/webm;codecs=opus','audio/ogg;codecs=opus'] (L38311) breaks recording on Safari/WKWebView if reordered; and it is not the composer mic — it stores an attachment rather than producing a transcript, so "merge the two voice paths" would replace a persisted staff voice message with text and lose the audio. Third, authority: `@Roles` on the controller is the only barrier between staff traffic and client chats (S-272), so the lane selector must enforce it on the server rather than by hiding the lane. Transport ranks below these but is real — per-chunk receipt verification and resumability must survive the merge, and a feed that polls every 10 seconds folded into a push/realtime chat changes delivery latency (S-272). And for the `maya-os-site` copy on the legacy МЭ proxy this is a rebuild, not a re-parent (S-100), with parity to be proven against a surface most people have never seen (S-282).
user_impact: Only staff notice, conditionally — all six rows are roleMode `staff`, so no client-facing capability is added or removed; clients see nothing change ONLY IF the lane selector inherits the staff role scope (see the security field), because the merged thread is the same shell clients use. The per-build reachability claim in the original is inverted and must be replaced. Production `app.html` already has a live, signposted entry: AStaffHome (L28695) renders an unconditional «Команда · Внутренний чат смены» row at L29169 calling `__meGo("team-chat")` → router screen `'team-chat'` (L39153) → ATeamChat, and `staff-home` is the staff cold-start screen (L5784). The adjacent code comment states outright that without this row the screen would be unreachable — i.e. the row is the entry, and it exists. So this merge is NOT "the first time the capability is reachable" for `app.html` staff and is not a discoverability fix for them; the only `app.html` mount that needs a hand-typed URL is the second, overlay ReactDOM root behind `?team=main` (L38331), whose anchor sits in the never-rendered AStaffDashboard (S-040/S-064). `?team=main` is also not a curiosity: since R12 the retired legacy proxy returns HTTP 410 `canonical_team_owner_required` with `url: https://malesthetic.pro/app/?team=main` as the advertised canonical entry. The other two builds are the broken ones, not working alternatives: `app-tenant.html` does have the primary-nav staff tab (STAFF_TABS index 3 → `'team-chat'`, L21844/L21963/L22018, S-142) and `maya-os-site/index.html` does have the AStaffHome row (L26344, hidden when `saasBusiness`, S-100), but both mount an ATeamChat whose transport is the legacy МЭ proxy `TC_PROXY = https://malesthetic.pro/app/api-proxy.php` (app-tenant L21008, maya-os-site L34866), and every `team_chat_*` action there now 410s. Only `app.html` is on the canonical `/team-communications/*` tenant API (L38226/L38241/L38303). Two user-visible changes the original omits: (1) delivery latency — the feed polls every 10 s today (L38314) and moving to push/realtime changes the characteristic staff expect (S-272); (2) voice notes are not simply "an input mode of the thread" — the team recorder produces a stored, chunk-uploaded audio attachment, while the assistant composer mic produces a transcript (S-282, S-100), so the casual framing is the exact naive merge S-282 warns loses the audio.
security_impact: The merge does not by itself weaken authority, but the original's reasoning for that is wrong in two places and its risk list is incomplete. The server-side gate is real and is not the only one: `team-communications.controller.ts` carries `@TenantScoped()` plus `@Roles(TENANT_OWNER, BUSINESS_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN, ADMINISTRATOR, STAFF)` (S-272) and every handler scopes on `a.tenantId!`, and the МЭ relay path re-checks the same role set in `canonical_team_communications.handle` before forwarding the caller's own bearer to port 3107 — so authority ultimately rests with the controller, but "the only load-bearing check" is inaccurate. Note the gate's shape: STAFF and every owner/admin role share one tenant-wide feed, so this is role-gating, not separation of duties; it does not become weaker, but it was never fine-grained. The claim that "the merge re-parents UI, not that gate" is contradicted by the evidence it cites: S-100 states explicitly that a merge here "is a rebuild, not a re-parent," because ATeamChat's rich client (hold-to-record with slide-to-cancel and swipe-up lock, chunked attachments with per-chunk receipt verification, media viewer, presence/typing, TCVoice playback) has no counterpart in AChat. Four things must be engineered, not assumed. (1) Lane role scope: what keeps staff traffic out of a client's view today is partly that staff chat is a physically separate screen or build, so the lane selector must inherit the server role scope or internal messages surface in a client's thread (S-272). (2) Provenance: that same separation is what stops a master pasting client PD into a thread they believe is internal; once the human lane and the MAYA lane share one shell, visible human-vs-assistant provenance becomes the 152-ФЗ control, not a cosmetic detail (S-142). (3) Voice-path substitution — omitted by the original and a real 152-ФЗ direction change: the team recorder stores audio, the composer mic yields a transcript, so folding staff voice notes into the composer path would route staff speech (which can name clients) through a transcription/LLM pipeline the internal lane deliberately avoids (S-282). (4) Live microphone: S-282 records that streams are torn down on unmount (L38314) and that hosting the recorder in a chat lane that mounts and unmounts with messages risks leaking a live mic — a privacy regression created by the merge itself. On multi-tenancy the original understates the gap and mislabels it as an optional upgrade: it is not only the `maya-os-site` copy on the legacy proxy — `app-tenant.html`, the tenant build, routes its primary-nav staff team tab through the same single-tenant `TC_PROXY` (L21008), and since R12 retired the PHP storage owner both copies get HTTP 410 `canonical_team_owner_required`. So for those two builds this is repair of a dead, un-tenant-scoped surface onto the `@TenantScoped` controller, not a bonus improvement available by re-routing; skipping it leaves them broken rather than merely leaky. No frozen limitation is contradicted (no claim is made about fail-closed 13/21, STEP_UP, Gate 10, approval separation-of-duties, or GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM).
